correctness.rationale: Exact Jensen-gap identity and nonnegative power-mean gap checked algebraically. Uniform inradius translation inclusion bounds the radial log ratios, the convex gauge is differentiable almost everywhere, and radial-area pushforward rigorously identifies H,Q,Phi. Taylor expansion gives q(q+1)/8 and coefficient (n+p)/8. Critical dominated convergence, coarse covariogram Lipschitz derivative, and fine quadratic limit are locally uniform. Quantitative bound Dp >= c p|x|^2/(1+p|x|) plus strict positivity away from zero proves entire-set Hausdorff localization. SymPy verified the scalar jet; finite square quadrature was only a diagnostic. No claim of C2 regularity is made.

originality.rationale: The principal 2026 theorem assumes a smooth boundary (C3 for the three phase limits; C2 for the Hessian), excluding every polytope. The present radial-gauge/Jensen-gap argument establishes a complete all-convex-body three-phase limit and a fixed-p Peano germ without those hypotheses. Closest accessible primary proofs and indexed mathematical records concern either smooth K or a different operator. No existing implication was located; possible nonindexed direct coverage is a residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact original 2026 three-phase theorem excludes polygons and polytopes by C3 regularity, a material limitation for projection geometry. Removing all boundary regularity for the entire convex-body class, including correct global sublevel localization and fixed-p Peano germ, closes a meaningful natural domain gap and connects smooth-covariogram asymptotics to nonsmooth convex geometry without assuming regularizing approximation.
